# Runtime transform first histories

These are informed studies, not blind benchmarks. Two separate packets retain
all original source, predictions, observer code, diagnostics and the original
test-source snapshot. All 16 baseline invocations refused. No program execution,
sampling or maximum-size quantum case was performed. The intended examples use
zero through three physical axes; none of their downstream expectations was
validated by these early refusals.

The first eight checks preserve five distinct obstacles: a forbidden generic
classical header, a finite static-argument boundary, a finite Nat-formal boundary,
four mistaken tuple argument wrappers and a phase gate used directly as an Op
provider. The original predictions expected later finite-profile refusals; the
earlier parser/header/provider failures remain unchanged.

The translations are separate sources, with explicit tuple grouping and a
phase-provider wrapper. Seven first cases are retained or repaired, and a new
coherent scalar/group case is added. All eight translation checks still stop at
finite Nat/static-argument boundaries. Their copied prediction dictionary has a
stale generic-classical entry and no dedicated coherent-scalar prediction. That
recording limitation is preserved; no missing prediction is reconstructed.

The first packet retains the complete immediate original directory tree except
the `translations-01` subtree. That excluded subtree is retained completely in
the separate second packet. Fixed-metadata USTAR/gzip archives retain all
71 unchanged files / 63,625 expanded bytes: first 36 / 36,763 and translations
35 / 26,862. `packets.json` binds every byte count, SHA-256 and original mode.
The existing 80-member, 5 MiB expanded and 2 MiB stored reader bounds apply
without increases. The four earlier general-static-runtime packets are unchanged.

Both captures observed dirty HEAD
`460f72e019885bd859686b6f4a8b265b40ab36fd`, CLI SHA-256
`ee67c0cb27748de6f7b13a4807eaf7ba8d96552816f5f0f23bc9cc1f0daf9c5b`
and kernel SHA-256
`54c9d60b80f67217abd95c8fe6ec1c06aa262e142d5e6db30f46a20cb90faf07`.
Executable and case-source hashes are stable within each retained window. The
dirty status strings and test snapshot are not complete compiler-source hashes
and are not a clean commit-to-binary build attestation.

The bounded passive reader never executes recorded commands, source or observer
code and never extracts archive members. It verifies complete inventories,
source/manifests, full streams, original observation order and retained identities.
This history does not establish current implementation correctness, native
acceptance, source/runtime preservation, QS/PR/quantitative RS/EXACT, Issue
completion or release readiness. Fresh candidate validation remains separate.
